svg.title: Echo and Rouw: a Partner’s Eigen, the Echo that tracks it, and the Rouw that outlives it
svg.desc: One Lid’s Echo of its Partner, from Sections II, IX.9, XV and XXVI of the Speelgoed. While the Relatie lives, the Partner’s Eigen x_j moves and the Echo E follows it by the delay filter, drawn in its first-order limit (no Traagheid, I = 0, and no colouring, β = 0): τ·dE/dt = x_j(t − δ) − E + υ. It hears every change late, by the Vertraging δ; it closes on it gradually, at the rate set by the Ontspanning τ; and it is never exact, because of the Vervorming υ. The distance between the Eigen and the Echo is the Echo gap, a real and queryable quantity. At t₀ the Relatie ends. The Partner’s last signals still arrive until t₀ + δ, and the Echo settles toward the last of them. From then on the Rouw is the one that looks: its signal x_R moves by its keeper’s own Vervorming at each of its looks and holds between them, so the Rouw drifts, more and more a record of the one that keeps it than of the one it lost. No live Eigen is left to compare it with, so its Echo gap cannot be read. No crossing can draw a Rouw out: it is permanent. The curves are a simulation of the equations with arbitrary values; they carry no scale.

§II · §IX.9 · §XV · §XXVI · RELATIES END; ECHOES DO NOT

τ · Ė = xⱼ(t − δ) − E + υ then τ · Ė = xR − E, xR (t₀ + δ) = xⱼ(t₀)
While the Relatie lives, the Echo hears each change late (δ), closes on it gradually (τ), and is never a clean copy (υ).
When it ends, the Rouw is the one that looks: its signal xR moves only at its own looks, and holds between them,
so it drifts, more a record of the one that keeps it than of the one it lost. Quiet is not gone: touch it, and it answers.
An Echo always outlives its Relatie. Rouw is permanent: no crossing can draw a Rouw out.
Drawn with no Traagheid (I = 0) and no colouring (β = 0). The curves simulate the filter with arbitrary values; they carry no scale.
